data.description:
## Description

**What**: A shared enforcement gate library (enforcement-gate.sh) and contract document that all gating hooks source to read enforcement.strategy and emit the HOOK_GATE: skipped log line uniformly.
**Why**: Without a single source of truth, ten+ hook scripts will each implement gate logic differently, producing drift that silently disables enforcement for individual rules and breaks audit criterion A.
**Scope**:
- IN: enforcement-gate.sh in plugins/dso/hooks/lib/ exposing _dso_enforcement_gate_check; contract doc at plugins/dso/hooks/lib/enforcement-gate-contract.md fixing log line shape (HOOK_GATE: skipped reason=enforcement.strategy=<value>), exit code, stderr/stdout channel; canonical list of which hooks gate vs always-on
- OUT: Modifying individual hooks to source the library (that is S2 scope); config key introduction (S1)

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, enforcement-gate.sh exists in plugins/dso/hooks/lib/ and exports _dso_enforcement_gate_check that: reads enforcement.strategy via read-config.sh, emits HOOK_GATE: skipped reason=enforcement.strategy=<value> to stderr when strategy is ci, exits 0 to allow the calling hook to short-circuit
  <- Satisfies: "PreToolUse hooks and .pre-commit-config.yaml entries read enforcement.strategy and short-circuit to no-op (with structured HOOK_GATE: skipped reason=enforcement.strategy=ci log)"
- When this story is complete, enforcement-gate-contract.md specifies the log line schema, exit codes, and the canonical list of gating hooks (test-gate, review-gate, test-quality-gate) vs always-on hooks (check-portability, check-shim-refs, check-contract-schemas, check-referential-integrity, check-plugin-self-ref, pre-commit-enforcement-boundary-check)
  <- Satisfies: "no enforcement bypass"
- When this story is complete, _dso_enforcement_gate_check defaults to local (strictest) when enforcement.strategy key is absent from dso-config.conf
  <- Satisfies: "enforcement.strategy (local|ci|both, default local) introduced"
- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic

## Considerations

- [Maintainability] Contract doc must enumerate always-on hooks explicitly so future hook authors know the policy
- [Security] Library must not silently fail if enforcement.strategy key is absent — must default to local (strictest)

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a plugin maintainer, I have a shared enforcement-gate library and contract that standardizes HOOK_GATE log schema across all hooks
